title: High Cyclomatic Complexity (The Indentation Pyramid)
pattern: Deeply nested control structures (nested `if`, `match`, `for`, and `if let` blocks) pushing execution logic 5+ levels deep inside a single function.
why_bad: High cognitive load and increased risk of silent logic errors. Invariants are scattered across several nesting levels, making it nearly impossible to trace the failure paths. The function lacks local reasoning; readers must keep the cumulative state of all parent branches in mind.
detection: Identify methods with nested blocks exceeding 3 levels of indentation. Look for multiple nested conditional statements and loops within a single function body.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Heterogeneous tree-traversal algorithms may naturally require several levels of matching and recursion, though these should still be kept as small as possible.
fix: Apply guard clauses (early returns on error/invalid states) to flatten the indentation hierarchy.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 17, "Unusual Control Structures"; *Robert C. Martin - Clean Code (2008)*, Chapter 3, "Functions".
